Cordis.metaDescription: Read "A Programming Paradigm for Spatiotemporal Composability" from zero: revertible effects and reactive coeffects.
Cordis.glossaryNote: The paper only includes concepts it introduces or gives special meaning to; general concepts are not repeated here.

glossary.desc: The ability to fully and safely revert a component's modifications to the shared environment when it is removed.
The ability of components to declare, discover, and resolve each other's dependencies in a structured, verifiable way.
Every context transformation explicitly provides an inverse; the runtime records and composes inverses, so uninstalling restores state.
A component declares a dependency spec; changes in dependency satisfaction automatically drive activation and deactivation.
∂Γ ≔ Γ × 𝔉Γ: the runtime context of current state plus accumulated recovery transformations.
Σ ≔ (k ∶ K) ⇀ 𝒱ₖ: a finite partial map from dependency keys to typed values.
A tuple of resolved dependency values, numbering a concrete dependency configuration of the target state.
Reload/Unload transitions in the async lifecycle — once entered, they run to completion.

Plugins.riskyBanner: This repository has been flagged as risky/suspicious (e.g. impersonating an official repo). Do not trust its download or install instructions.
Plugins.installProfileNote: The name after --profile is a profile name you choose yourself — swap in whichever one you use.
Plugins.installGitNote: The author hasn't published to npm, so this command installs from git source. pnpm ≥ 10 refuses to run a git dependency's prepare script until you grant it, so your first install needs an allowBuilds entry in that profile's pnpm-workspace.yaml — which means letting this package's code run on your machine. Pin a #commit while you're at it.
Plugins.installReleaseNote: This command uses the unique uploaded GitHub Release .tgz whose asset name, release tag, package name, and package version agree. dshfind does not download, unpack, or execute the asset while probing; review the publisher and release before installing.
Plugins.installBuildNote: This is a bundle, but the author hasn't published to npm, the package entry points at build output (lib/ or dist/), and the repo has no prepare script. Installing straight from git only pulls uncompiled source and the entry won't be there at load time. Build it locally first, then install it by path:
Plugins.installNoneManifest: There is no package.json at the repo root, so dsh plugin add fails outright.
Plugins.installNoneBundle: The package.json declares no dsh.bundle, so even once installed into a profile it is never assembled.
Plugins.installNoneHint: It may be an index list, documentation, a standalone app, or still in development — check the repo README for how to use it.
Plugins.installUnknown: We haven't probed this repo's install method yet — see the repo README.
Plugins.detailPinned: Pinned full score by the editors.
Plugins.detailSuspicious: Possible star inflation — pending manual review
Plugins.shareDesc: Drop it into your README — it links back to this page.
